why: Leaf 40's descriptor writes the singular and leaf 1's index the plural, of one plate. A slip of the pen, not two works. Both spellings stay as written in the transcription; this only makes the link work from either.

The Art Institute catalogues the 1920 plate under an English title where the Met and the Hoppers use the French. Same date, same medium, and the Hoppers' own title is the French one. A judgement, not a slip.

The ledger's title for the plate at leaf 30; both the Met and the Art Institute catalogue a 1918 etching as 'Night on the El Train'. The elevated railway is the same railway, but the two titles are not the same words and this is our identification, not theirs.

Book II leaf 95 heads the canvas « Night Hawks » at 33 x 60, dates it finished 21 January 1942, and books its sale to the Chicago Art Institute on 13 May 1942; the Art Institute catalogues a 1942 oil of 33 1/8 x 60 in. as « Nighthawks », accession 1942.51, and gives its provenance as consigned to Rehn and sold to the museum in 1942. One canvas and one sale, written in two words on the leaf and in one by the museum.

Book I leaf 55 heads the picture « Ex Lax », after the brand on the shop window, and describes it as « Drugstore. Side walk, red & green drug store bottles »; its size, 29 x 40, and its passage from John T. Spaulding to the Boston museum are those of the painting the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston catalogues as Drug Store (1927). A judgement from outside the leaf, so likely rather than certain.

The ledger says so itself. Book I leaf 58 heads the 35 x 60 canvas « 7" Ave. Shops », and the list of museum purchases a few leaves on writes « Whitney Amer. Museum - 7" Ave. Shops. Spring 1930. Gallery opened Nov. 1931. Otherwise known as Early Sunday Morning », which is the title the Whitney catalogues it under.
The numeral written as a figure on the leaf and spelled out in the Whitney's catalogue; one title.
Book I leaf 58 writes « Light House » as two words; the Met catalogues the 1929 oil as one. A spelling, not two works.

Book I leaf 52 heads the 1925 canvas « House by a Railroad »; the list of museum purchases in the same volume writes « Modern Museum - Given by Stephen Clark - House by R.R. », and MoMA catalogues that gift as House by the Railroad. The article differs, not the picture.
Book III leaf 107 spells the saint « Estoban »; the Met catalogues the 1946 Saltillo watercolour as Church of San Esteban. A spelling, not two works.
Book I leaf 41 writes « Les Poilhus » for the etching the Whitney catalogues as Les Poilus. The misspelling stays in the transcription; this only lets the link work.
Book I leaf 24 runs the medium into the title line; the plate is Railroad Crossing, catalogued under that title by the Met, the Art Institute, the Whitney and MoMA.
Book I leaf 12 writes « Rail Road » as two words in the etchings section; MoMA catalogues the 1922 etching as The Railroad. A spelling, not two works.

Book II leaf 27 heads the picture « N.Y. Movie House », 32 x 40, finished 29 January 1939 and bought by Stephen C. Clark; Book I's list of reproductions writes « Movie House - the Mus. of Mod. Art », and MoMA catalogues the 1939 canvas as New York Movie. The size, the year and the museum agree; the title is a judgement, so likely rather than certain.
